correctness.rationale: Verified the original five cosine thresholds are E<C<D<B<M in a 0<phi<pi/10 chamber; vertical edge crossing plus 0/2 crossings per pentagonal cap gives interval counts (4,5,6,7,6,5). Haar z=|u3| uniform on [0,1], conditional t=h z/sqrt(1-z²) CDF q/sqrt(h²+q²). Its primitive is F_h(theta)=asin(sin(theta)/sqrt(1+h²)); integration gives all four Δ_j formulas and total 1 with strictly positive interval measures for every h>0. Independently implemented original fifteen prism-edge intersection test and 210,000 random Gaussian normals at each h=0.15, sin(pi/5), 2.2; histograms agreed within ~0.0032, and only 4–7 sides observed. Exact edge-angle mean and endpoint Taylor coefficients agree. Monte Carlo supports but does not prove continuous/unbounded h or positivity; those follow from threshold/analytic derivation.

value.rationale: A regular pentagonal prism is a canonical uniform solid. The entire four-mass central section-type law for all positive aspect ratios distinguishes quadrilateral/pentagon/hexagon/heptagon cases; the strictly positive heptagon probability has nontrivial different flat/tall degeneration exponents. The exact function is useful for random-section combinatorics and orientation stereology and is not mechanically determined by known expected side counts or solid widths.
residual_risks: A special geometric family, not arbitrary polyhedra; this limitation does not erase the natural full classification.

final_claim: For every h>0, a uniformly oriented central plane of the regular pentagonal prism with circumradius 1 and half-height h cuts exactly 4,5,6,7 edges almost surely, all with positive probability given by four inverse-sine increment formulas Δ_j, δ=π/10. At h=sin(π/5), masses ≈(0.2487718901,0.4957829106,0.1877211225,0.0677240769); the heptagon mass is Θ(h²) as h→0 and Θ(h^-1) as h→∞; exact mean by sum of edge spherical crossing angles.
limitations: No uniqueness of maximizing aspect ratio claimed; strict positivity and tail exponents are analytic, not simulation-based.
